answer: In an agent economy, modulated retroreflector interrogation binds each identity to a corner-cube prism with an electro-optic shutter. A verifier sweeps a nonce-encoded laser across sectors while the shutter modulates a signed nonce via a trellis code onto the reflected beam, using range delay and angle to expose co-located clones. Faking identities requires separate optics and spaced sites per node, yet swaying branches in a grove or dense fog can sever line of sight for honest agents.
